matrix_target_rows.user_job: Create, send, pay, and cancel invoices
Preview, create, and post an FX revaluation to the general ledger.

normative_interpretation.MUST: Directly established behavior restated without source identity or implementation.
normative_interpretation.SHOULD: Evidence-backed preference only; none was established.
normative_interpretation.NOT_ESTABLISHED: Unknown, unproved, explicitly limited, or non-transferable behavior that must not be inferred.

MUST.requirement: The revaluation flow must capture an organisational ledger context and reporting or posting date before retrieving balances.
Creating revaluation journals must require journal-write authority distinct from permission to inspect the revaluation record.
The flow must enumerate balance-sheet accounts held in a currency different from the base currency, while excluding group, stock, and same-currency accounts.
Each eligible row must expose the foreign-currency balance, current base-currency balance, current exchange rate, new exchange rate, new base-currency balance, and calculated gain or loss.

The new base-currency balance must be calculated from the unchanged foreign-currency amount and an exchange rate effective for the selected date; gain or loss must equal the difference from the current base-currency balance.
A row with no foreign-currency balance or no base-currency balance must be handled separately so a residual carrying balance can be cleared instead of being processed as an ordinary revaluation.
Organisational ledger context and date must be present, and the rounding-loss allowance must satisfy 0 <= allowance < 1.
Submission must remove rows without a gain or loss and must fail when no gain-or-loss row remains.
When no qualifying balances exist, the actor must receive feedback stating either that no outstanding items require revaluation or that none were found.
Journal creation must be blocked unless an unrealised gain or loss account is configured.
Successful action must create attributable multi-currency journal entries linked to the revaluation record, with balanced debit and credit totals.
Success feedback must provide access to the ordinary revaluation journal and, when one was created, the zero-balance journal.
The record must locate posted linked journals, determine whether their booked gain or loss equals the revaluation total, and independently determine whether reversals have posted.
A reversal action must create draft reversals only for posted linked journals that have no reversal; an existing draft reversal must prevent duplicate creation and be surfaced to the actor.

The flow must distinguish the observed draft and submitted record conditions, linked-journal condition, and draft-reversal condition wherever their corresponding behavior is available; no additional transition ordering is implied.

NOT_ESTABLISHED.requirement: Final posting orchestration, exchange-rate provenance, retry idempotency, concurrent execution behavior, approval separation, durable recovery, accessibility, and the complete authorization scope are not established.
Organisational ledger scope does not establish any site-level access model, direct-object concealment, privacy boundary, or supported-living workflow.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Balance retrieval cannot proceed until both organisational ledger context and date are supplied; omission produces validation feedback.
An actor able only to inspect the record cannot create its journals without the separately required journal-write authority.
Given a mixture of eligible and excluded accounts, only foreign-currency balance-sheet accounts outside the group, stock, and same-currency exclusions appear.

Every eligible row displays all six observed financial values, and recalculation preserves the foreign amount, uses the date-effective rate, and derives gain or loss from the current and new base amounts.
A row lacking either observed balance is routed through the residual-clearing branch rather than ordinary revaluation handling.
Negative and values greater than or equal to one are rejected for rounding-loss allowance; zero and values below one satisfy the stated numeric boundary when other mandatory inputs are present.
Submission removes zero-gain-or-loss rows, and submission fails when that removal leaves no gain-or-loss row.
An empty qualifying result produces one of the two observed no-work or no-results messages.
Journal creation cannot proceed when the unrealised gain or loss account is absent.
Successful creation yields linked, attributable, multi-currency entries whose debit and credit totals balance, and reports the ordinary journal plus any applicable zero-balance journal.
For posted linked journals, the record can separately report gain-or-loss agreement with the revaluation total and posted-reversal status.

A posted linked journal without a reversal can receive one draft reversal; a journal that is not posted or already has a reversal does not receive another, and an existing draft is disclosed as the duplication blocker.
The observed draft, submitted, linked-journal, and draft-reversal conditions are distinguishable without implying unobserved final-posting states.

MUST.requirement: An actor must be able to create an invoice in Draft and subsequently submit it.
Draft, Submitted, Unpaid, Partly Paid, Paid, Overdue, and Cancelled must be represented as distinct states; no transition order beyond separately observed actions is inferred.
Submission must apply an approval control and produce accounting effects; stock effects must also apply when the invoice bears stock.
A submitted invoice must offer payment capture and payment-request actions.

A payment request must support an attached invoice or payment link, must be handed off only after the initiating change commits, and must suppress duplicate outbound hand-offs for that observed request.
Cancellation must reverse relevant effects, cancel associated ledger entries, and change the invoice state to Cancelled.

NOT_ESTABLISHED.requirement: Target-specific site access, privacy, direct-object concealment, retry behavior beyond the observed send hand-off, accessibility, and supported-living terminology are not established.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A newly created invoice is Draft, can later be submitted, and each of the seven observed states is distinguishable.
Submission passes through the approval control, produces accounting effects, and applies stock effects only where stock is involved.
A submitted invoice exposes both payment capture and payment-request actions.
A payment request can carry either the invoice attachment or a payment link; no outbound hand-off occurs before commit, and duplicate hand-offs for that observed request are suppressed.
Cancellation reverses applicable effects, cancels associated ledger entries, and leaves the invoice in Cancelled.

MUST.requirement: Draft, Validated, Closed, and Abandoned must be represented as distinct customer-invoice states; no additional equivalence or transition ordering is implied.
Invoice creation must begin in Draft.
An invoice that is paid must be explicitly closed.
An unpaid invoice must support abandonment with a cancellation event, while correction of a paid invoice must use a distinct credit-note path rather than that same cancellation path.
Successful email delivery must increment the invoice send counter and emit a delivery event.
Payment creation must distribute amounts across invoices and close each invoice that becomes paid.

NOT_ESTABLISHED.requirement: Exact equivalence among abandonment, cancellation, credit-note correction, and any target lifecycle is not established.
Site access, privacy, direct-object concealment, retry behavior, and accessibility parity are not established.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A newly created invoice is Draft, and Draft, Validated, Closed, and Abandoned remain distinguishable states.
When an invoice becomes paid, it is explicitly Closed.
An unpaid invoice can be abandoned and emits the observed cancellation event; a paid invoice is corrected through a separate credit-note path.
On successful email delivery, the send counter increments and a delivery event is emitted.
A payment can be distributed across multiple invoices, and every invoice made paid by that allocation is closed.

MUST.requirement: Create, mail, delete, deliver, write-off, and payment-history actions must each be subject to an authorization check, without prescribing roles or an authorization model.
Invoice creation and its related journal work must succeed or fail as one unit.
Invoice email delivery must support later transport hand-off, may include a PDF attachment, and must mark the invoice delivered only after transport succeeds.
Only one delivery operation may proceed for an invoice at a time, and duplicate delivery attempts must be rejected.
Payment allocation must update the invoice paid amount.
Deletion must evaluate a stable invoice state and must be rejected when payments or applied credits exist.

NOT_ESTABLISHED.requirement: This adjacent slice does not establish a submitted-invoice cancellation or reversal lifecycle; it establishes only observed deletion and write-off behavior.
No organisational-partitioning abstraction, site, access, privacy, or supported-living semantics may be inferred from this packet.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Each of the six listed actions invokes its relevant authorization guard; no particular role structure is assumed.
A failure in either invoice creation or related journal work leaves neither side partially completed.
Delivery may be handed off for later transport and may include a PDF, but delivered status is recorded only following successful transport.
A second delivery attempt is rejected while or after the protected delivery operation makes it a duplicate; no concurrent-execution model beyond this safeguard is inferred.
Allocating a payment changes the invoice paid amount accordingly.
Deletion is rejected, and the invoice retained, when a payment or applied credit exists.
